question: Should OpenClaw add a supported absolute-deadline checkpoint-warning contract, and if so should it be a shared sub-agent default only or also a native per-spawn API despite ACP’s current timeout-override boundary?
rationale: The request is a new lifecycle capability and potentially a new configuration/API surface; source and docs show native and ACP timeout controls are not currently symmetric, so implementation cannot safely choose the permanent public contract unilaterally.

options.title: Design one shared warning contract
options.body: Specify a documented best-effort warning and its native/ACP guarantees before implementing a single coherent configuration surface.

options.title: Defer to stall recovery only
options.body: Keep absolute wall-clock deadlines unchanged and treat inactivity-based nudge/kill work in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/39305 as the supported recovery direction.

options.title: Adopt a native-only warning
options.body: Expose a warning only for native sub-agent runs and explicitly document that ACP runs retain hard-timeout behavior.

recommendation.title: Design one shared warning contract
recommendation.body: Specify a documented best-effort warning and its native/ACP guarantees before implementing a single coherent configuration surface.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal spans both native and ACP sub-agent lifecycle paths that must share the decision.
